script.text: A fluent answer can sound certain even when the model is guessing. Jev takes a different route: typed probabilities for a bounded decision. In the evaluation harness I have been building, that makes the real work visible. First, inspect the score. A 0.81 result can route differently from one at 0.54. Then apply a pre-authorized policy: route, review, or stop. Finally, keep exceptions and irreversible actions with a person, and retain the versioned receipt. The value is practical: operators can see the score, the threshold, the owner, and the evidence behind the handoff. Jev’s launch does not prove production reliability, and my current harness remains mock-qualified with live provider use on hold. Use the field guide as a review test. Before any score moves work, ask what threshold applies, who owns the exception, and which receipt remains. Governed automation begins when uncertainty is visible enough to route, review, and refuse.

prior_script.text: A score is not a decision. Read the signal, apply the policy, and keep a human owner visible. Route the exception. Make uncertainty visible enough to act.
